title: Building a Smooth 60fps Vertical Text Ticker in CSS
description: Designing a lightweight, zero-JS vertical text marquee with CSS keyframe animation and zero horizontal layout shift on mobile.
content: Adding dynamic tagline animations to a developer portfolio header creates instant engagement. However, implementing smooth vertical text tickers using JavaScript intervals often causes layout jitter, re-renders, and horizontal overflow on mobile screens.
### The Challenge

Creating an infinite vertical scrolling text ticker in React that transitions smoothly between multiple phrases with controllable display intervals, without triggering JS re-render loops or pushing flexbox parents beyond mobile screen boundaries.
### The Solution
### Key Takeaways

CSS keyframe animations outperform JavaScript interval timers for continuous UI motion. Combining CSS transforms with defensive flexbox bounds guarantees high-performance 60fps motion without layout overflow on small screens.

title: Building a Chat-Inspired Contact Page with Background AJAX Dispatch
description: Designing a seamless, chat-bubble contact experience with background AJAX form dispatch, real-time loading feedback, and zero page redirects.
content: Traditional web contact forms often rely on mailto links or heavy external redirects that break user flow. To create a modern, frictionless experience on my portfolio, I designed a chat-inspired contact component with direct background AJAX email dispatch.
### The Challenge

Delivering a direct contact channel that feels as responsive as a messaging app, ensuring user messages land straight in my email inbox without triggering full-page browser redirects, popups, or requiring visitors to launch desktop mail apps.
### The Solution

I engineered a chat-interface component using React, TypeScript, and FormSubmit AJAX dispatch:
1. **Background AJAX Delivery**: Sent form payloads via `fetch()` to an endpoint returning JSON responses asynchronously, preventing page reloads.
2. **Micro-Interactions & Loading States**: Replaced the static submit button with a sleek icon-only toggle (`<LuSend />` to `<FaSpinner className="animate-spin" />`) while disabling fields during dispatch.
3. **Conversational Feedback**: Rendered an in-chat success bubble upon resolution to confirm message delivery before resetting state.

```tsx
await fetch('https://formsubmit.co/ajax/delatorrenelson127@gmail.com', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ email, message })
});
```
### Key Takeaways
Designing contact forms as conversational chat interfaces reduces user friction. Combining background AJAX fetch with visual micro-feedback yields a native app-like messaging experience.

title: Implementing Runtime Feature Flags & Live Syncing in React
description: Designing a lightweight, runtime-configurable feature flag engine for static web applications with live auto-syncing.
content: Building static applications deployed to edge CDNs is fantastic for speed, but toggling features or hiding draft UI components usually requires a full rebuild and redeployment pipeline.
### The Challenge

Designing a dynamic feature toggle system that reads runtime configuration (`portfolio.config.json`) in a static React app without breaking layout, while ensuring configuration changes update live without requiring manual browser page refreshes.
### The Solution
### Key Takeaways
Runtime configuration decouples deployment from feature rollout. Polling combined with event listeners makes static React apps feel as responsive as server-side dynamic applications.

title: Cloudflare: Too Many Redirects Error when Proxying
description: Troubleshooting SSL/TLS encryption modes and flexible proxy settings causing infinite redirect loops.
content: When proxying web traffic through Cloudflare for a client application, I ran into the infamous `ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS` browser error. The web server was running Nginx with an SSL certificate issued via Let's Encrypt, yet any HTTPS request triggered an infinite redirect loop.
### The Challenge

The issue stemmed from a mismatch between Cloudflare's SSL/TLS encryption mode and the backend server configuration. Cloudflare was set to **Flexible SSL mode**, connecting to the origin server over unencrypted HTTP (port 80). However, our Nginx configuration enforced a strict HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect (`return 301 https://$host$request_uri;`). This created an endless loop where Nginx kept redirecting HTTP to HTTPS while Cloudflare kept querying Nginx via HTTP.
### The Solution

To resolve this, I updated the Cloudflare SSL/TLS encryption setting from **Flexible** to **Full (Strict)**, ensuring Cloudflare establishes an encrypted HTTPS connection to the origin server using valid SSL certificates.

Additionally, I verified Nginx proxy headers to ensure `X-Forwarded-Proto` was correctly passed:
```nginx
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
```
### Key Takeaways
Always align your CDN proxy SSL mode with your origin server's HTTPS enforcement policies. Using Full (Strict) mode ensures end-to-end security while eliminating infinite redirection loops.

title: Up and Running with AWS EC2
description: Setting up elastic compute cloud instances, security groups, and automated deployment pipelines.
content: Deploying scalable cloud compute instances is a fundamental milestone in full-stack web engineering. Recently, I set up a dedicated AWS EC2 architecture for hosting containerized Node.js applications.
### The Challenge
The main challenge was configuring a secure, production-ready compute instance without exposing sensitive ports or leaving the server vulnerable to unauthorized access and unexpected reboots.
### The Solution

I provisioned an Ubuntu Server 22.04 LTS instance and configured least-privilege AWS Security Groups:
- **SSH (Port 22)**: Restricted strictly to static administrator IP ranges.
- **HTTP (Port 80) & HTTPS (Port 443)**: Open to public web traffic (`0.0.0.0/0`).

After connecting via SSH, I set up Docker and systemd services for automated recovery on reboot:
```bash
sudo systemctl enable docker
sudo systemctl start docker
```
### Key Takeaways
Never expose SSH ports globally. Always implement the principle of least privilege in security groups and rely on systemd daemons for uptime reliability.

title: Up and Running with AWS VPC
description: Configuring custom virtual private clouds, subnets, route tables, and NAT gateways.
content: Building production cloud infrastructure requires a solid networking foundation. I designed a custom AWS Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) with isolated public and private subnets.
### The Challenge
Designing a network architecture that keeps backend database servers completely isolated from direct public internet access while still allowing them to fetch security updates and packages.
### The Solution

I structured a custom VPC (`10.0.0.0/16`) with multi-AZ public subnets (`10.0.1.0/24`, `10.0.2.0/24`) and private subnets (`10.0.10.0/24`, `10.0.20.0/24`).

To grant private instances outbound internet access without accepting inbound traffic, I deployed a NAT Gateway in the public subnet and pointed the private route table's default route (`0.0.0.0/0`) to the NAT Gateway.
### Key Takeaways
Separating public web nodes from private database networks dramatically reduces attack surface while maintaining outbound patch automation.

title: Dynamically Load Ansible Inventory with EC2 IP
description: Automating dynamic server inventory discovery for configuration management across cloud environments.
content: Automating dynamic server inventory discovery for configuration management across cloud environments.
### The Challenge
Manually updating static Ansible inventory files whenever AWS EC2 instances scale, terminate, or restart with new IP addresses is error-prone and unmaintainable in dynamic cloud environments.
### The Solution

I integrated the `amazon.aws.aws_ec2` inventory plugin by creating an `aws_ec2.yaml` configuration for automated host discovery based on resource tags:
```yaml
plugin: amazon.aws.aws_ec2
regions:
  - ap-southeast-1
keyed_groups:
  - key: tags.Environment
    prefix: env
  - key: tags.Role
    prefix: role
```

Running `ansible-inventory -i aws_ec2.yaml --graph` dynamically grouped hosts (`env_production`, `role_webserver`), eliminating hardcoded IPs from Playbooks.
### Key Takeaways
Infrastructure automation thrives on metadata and tagging. Dynamic inventory plugins eliminate manual upkeep and scale seamlessly as cloud nodes scale.

title: Generate Terraform from existing AWS infrastructure
description: Importing legacy cloud resources into infrastructure-as-code state files seamlessly.
content: Importing legacy cloud resources into infrastructure-as-code state files seamlessly.
### The Challenge

Managing cloud resources that were manually created through the AWS Console creates drift and lack of version control. Transitioning legacy infrastructure into Terraform without causing downtime or resource re-creation is critical.
### The Solution

Using Terraform 1.5+ declarative `import` blocks allowed clean resource mapping into state:
```hcl
import {
  to = aws_s3_bucket.portfolio_assets
  id = "my-portfolio-assets-bucket"
}
```

I then ran `terraform plan -generate-config-out=generated_resources.tf` to generate HCL configurations, which I refactored into modular, version-controlled IaC code.
### Key Takeaways
Manual cloud changes are technical debt. Declarative Terraform imports turn legacy infrastructure into version-controlled, repeatable environments.

title: My First Commit
description: This is my first commit to my portfolio website. Excited to share my software engineering journey.
content: Initiating the codebase for my personal portfolio application! As a developer passionate about intuitive user experiences and clean code, building a tailored digital workspace has been a top priority.
### The Challenge
Designing a modern portfolio that isn't just a static resume, but an interactive, fast, and maintainable web app showcasing projects, technical skills, and dev logs.
### The Solution

I architected the application with a modern frontend stack:
- **Vite & React 19**: Fast module reloading and modular component architecture.
- **TypeScript**: Strict type safety across components and data schemas.
- **Tailwind CSS v4 & DaisyUI 5**: Custom CSS-first design system with theme toggling.
```bash
npx create-vite portfolio --template react-ts
```
### Key Takeaways
Building a personal developer site is a continuous engineering effort. Prioritize performance, component modularity, and clean structure from day one.
